182	    def assign_attrs(self, elem: Element, attrs_string: str, *, strict: bool = False) -> str:
183	        """ Assign `attrs` to element.
184	
185	        If the `attrs_string` has an extra closing curly brace, the remaining text is returned.
186	
187	        The `strict` argument controls whether to still assign `attrs` if there is a remaining `}`.
188	        """
189	        attrs, remainder = get_attrs_and_remainder(attrs_string)
190	        if strict and remainder:
191	            return remainder
192	
193	        for k, v in attrs:
194	            if k == '.':
195	                # add to class
196	                cls = elem.get('class')
197	                if cls:
198	                    elem.set('class', '{} {}'.format(cls, v))
199	                else:
200	                    elem.set('class', v)
201	            elif v is None:
202	                # assign a valueless attribute. Maintain the historic
203	                # `key="key"` representation only for known boolean
204	                # attributes (which differ per output format). For any
205	                # other attribute, preserve what the user provided by
206	                # keeping the value as `None`, which the serializer
207	                # renders as the bare attribute name.
208	                name = self.sanitize_name(k)
209	                if name.lower() in BOOLEAN_ATTRIBUTES.get(self.md.output_format, frozenset()):
210	                    elem.set(name, name)
211	                else:
212	                    elem.set(name, None)
213	            else:
214	                # assign attribute `k` with `v`
215	                elem.set(self.sanitize_name(k), v)
216	        # The text that we initially over-matched will be put back.
217	        return remainder

issue_asks: A valueless id should behave as if no id was given, so the normal slug is generated
The fix must work with and without a [TOC] marker
Headings with a real id such as `# Title {#my-id}` must keep working unchanged

findings.problem: `not el.attrib.get("id")` also treats an empty-string id (`{id=""}`) as missing, so a slug is now generated where the old code kept the empty id. This is arguably better, but it is a behaviour change beyond the issue and has no test. Separately, `used_ids` (line 391-392) can contain `None` for a bare id. That is harmless because `unique` only does membership checks.
findings.evidence: Static read only. toc.py:391-392 and 403, plus attr_list.py:201-212, where `elem.set(name, None)` is used for valueless non-boolean attributes.

I could not approve this because no command could run in this session. The Bash sandbox failed to start (socat not installed), and bypassing it was disallowed. I did not run the test suite or any probe of my own, and by the rules that means I can't approve. This is not a rejection of the change.

From reading the code, the fix looks correct and in the right place. `attr_list` stores a bare `{id}` as `None` for non-boolean attributes (attr_list.py:201-212). The old `"id" not in el.attrib` check then skipped slug generation, and `unescape(el.attrib["id"])` at toc.py:420 raised the TypeError. The new check `not el.attrib.get("id")` generates the slug in that case, which matches the issue's expectation. A real id such as `{#my-id}` is still preserved. The `None` that can end up in `used_ids` is harmless because `unique` only does membership checks.

The two new tests, `testBareIdAttribute` and `testBareIdAttributeWithTOCMarker`, match the issue's scenarios. Nothing was deleted or loosened. The one side effect is that `{id=""}` now also gets a generated slug. It is probably fine but untested.

Please re-run this review where the sandbox works. It should run the full suite and try these inputs:
- Duplicate bare ids, `# a {id}` twice, which should give `a` and `a_1`.
- `# a {id=""}`.
- `# a {id}` after an earlier `# a`.
- A bare id with `permalink` or `anchorlink` enabled.
